spiritual_reading:
When the Divine established the ordered levels of being, it arranged degree upon degree, and also set subordinate degrees within higher ones, so that each lower plane might be held in place by what is above it. The outermost governing degree consisted of a sufficient set of fundamental evils and falsities in their active and receptive modes, which together form the first boundary of disorder.

This is why degree was fastened to degree: the entire complex of those evils and falsities was attached to a sufficient set of enlightened human faculties proceeding from the Divine Human, so that the whole opposition might be gathered, restrained, and held within fixed limits; for all hostility against good and truth is interwoven into such ultimates and can be bound there.

Within that same ordering there was also a sufficient complement of operative powers from the Divine proceeding that gives life and motion, because every structure of heaven and the church depends on these for its support and continuity. Here the text becomes uncertain, but it appears to indicate that these primary supports were acknowledged first, and that other supporting powers were established in a following order beneath them.

And there is One who descends to the higher interior degrees that govern what is beneath. This One, who is the supreme authority of Divine truth united with Divine good, is present within the inmost of the whole ordered creation and holds all things together from within.

fills.notes: The substrate sense here is an impersonal ordering of supports: first the primary five are established, and then it is said that they were “heard” or “acknowledged.” The phrase needs to yield “it being … heard him too,” i.e., the edifice depends on them, “as they heard” him. This keeps the cosmological-register verb of perception without introducing exhortation.

The passage contrasts the first supports with what follows: “the others … after them.” The spiritual context requires a subsequent order of subordinate supporters established beneath the first. “others who came” provides that sequential, structural sense (procession and ordering) without later community language.

The One “came to” an interior height governing the firmaments. In the substrate this is descent or approach into the higher structural degrees. “the heights, to” fits the required motion into the upper interiors while remaining cosmological and non-devotional.
A minimal connective is demanded to bind “firmaments above” to the following relative clause “which is in one zone.”

The spiritual sense identifies the supreme authority present within the inmost. The clause requires a verb of being with an inward abiding. “exists and dwells” preserves impersonal cosmological presence (immanence) rather than a salvific visitation.

The final gap must name the interior-most region “of the universe” where this One is present. The correspondential requirement is the inmost plane that holds all from within; “inmost depth” states that function in oldest-layer register (structural interiority).

assessment: Most lacunae can be restored at the level of structural correspondential requirements: ordering degree upon degree, primary supports, subsequent supports, and an inmost governing presence. Exact surface wording in ¶4–¶5 remains only moderately constrained, but the demanded functions (acknowledgement of the first supports; later supports following; descent to higher interiors; inmost indwelling) allow coherent restorations in the oldest cosmological register.
